findings.title: allowedIss (and jti/sub/nonce) accepted via loose element match when token claim is an array
findings.evidence: The scalar-claim validators for iss (line 475), jti (467), sub (479) and nonce (483) are registered without the array flag, yet validateClaimValues matches loosely: `if (!values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v))))` (line 159) passes as soon as ANY element matches an allowed value. In verifyToken, a token-supplied array is always normalized into a candidate list (`const arrayValue = Array.isArray(value)` line 211; `const values = arrayValue ? value : [value]` line 212), the element-wise type check at line 221 accepts an array of strings, and line 226 then applies the `.some()` predicate - so a JWT with `iss: ["https://attacker.example/", "https://trusted-issuer"]` (RFC 7519 requires iss to be a single string) is fully accepted because one element equals the configured allowedIss. Only aud is flagged `array: true` (line 471); for iss the flag is purely cosmetic, and the 'None of ...' message at line 157 confirms the partial-match semantics. The advisory exploit path (GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8 / CVE-2025-30144) is the get-jwks pattern: the verifier's key fetcher resolves the JWKS from the token's iss domain, so an attacker serves their own JWKS, signs a forged token whose iss array contains both their domain and the trusted issuer, and the verifier accepts attacker-signed payloads because the issuer allow-list check passes on the matching element. Fixed upstream in fast-jwt 5.0.6 (commit cc26b1d) by requiring `values.every(...)` for scalar claims and routing arrays only through the `array`-flagged validator.

findings.title: Array payload silently skips every claim validator (exp/nbf/iss/aud/jti/nonce bypass)
findings.evidence: A JWT whose payload is a JSON array (e.g. `[]` or `["x"]`) passes the decoder's object check because `typeof [] === 'object'` with no Array.isArray guard (src/decoder.js:38), and then in verifyToken the guard `if (!(claim in payload)) { continue }` (lines 216-218) is false for every string claim of an array (`'exp' in [] === false`), so each validator registered at lines 441-484 (nbf, exp, maxAge, jti, aud, iss, sub, nonce) is silently skipped. Only the signature check (line 139) runs, so any validly signed token - e.g. one minted with a shared HS256 secret or by a sibling service - is accepted regardless of expiration, not-before, issuer, audience or jti constraints; a correctly-signed `["x"]` payload verifies while the equivalent object payload is correctly rejected as expired. `requiredClaims` (lines 198-204) is the only guard but is opt-in. Fixed upstream in fast-jwt 6.3.0 (CVE-2026-107723 / GHSA-5hjw-83fp-phq9) by rejecting array payloads in the decoder.
